met_analysis:
The very severe cyclonic storm “Arnab” [Pronunciation :Ornab] over Westcentral Bay of Bengal moved nearly west-northwestwards with a speed of 20 kmph during past 6 hours, and lies centered at 0830 hrs IST of today, the 27th October, 2026 over the same region near latitude 16.0°N and longitude 84.3°E, 220 km south- southeast of Vishakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 240 km east-southeast of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 340 km east-southeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 370 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha), 410 km east of Bapatla (Andhra Pradesh) and 1030 km west-northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman Islands). It is very likely to move west-northwestwards till evening of 27th October. Thereafter, it is very likely to move northwestwards and cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 125-135 kmph gusting to 150 kmph by forenoon of 28th October, 2026.
A trough runs from southwest Bay of Bengal off Sri Lanka coast to centre of very severe cyclonic storm “Arnab” and extends upto 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The cyclonic circulation over Southwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining south coastal Tamil Nadu extending upto 3.1 km above mean sea level has merged with the above trough.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over north Haryana now lies over northwest Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood between 3.1 & 4.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood at 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 73°E to the north of Lat. 28°N persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over southeast Uttar Pradesh & adjoining Bihar persists and now seen at 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The trough from Lakshadweep Area to the cyclonic circulation over Southwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining south coastal Tamil Nadu across South Kerala extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
